documentation: Discrimination probes. A conformance table that every plausible implementation passes proves nothing — it is decoration. Each probe is a deliberately WRONG implementation, and the runner requires it to fail an EXACT set of case ids, not 'at least one'. An exact set is what turns the table into a measurement: it says which rows carry which hazard, and it goes red both when the corpus stops catching a mistake AND when a row starts failing for a reason nobody intended. The control is not optional: without an implementation that passes everything, the mutants prove only that the port is broken. Expected failures are computed as must_fail MINUS the cases that language skips.

probes.summary: When building the request body, drop any key whose value is null instead of emitting it.
probes.hazard: Absent versus null. This is the single mistake a port is most likely to make by accident, because it is what JSON.stringify does to undefined and what a naive dict comprehension does to None. Every row carrying an unset max_output_tokens catches it.

probes.summary: Filter the optional request-body keys on falsiness instead of on nullity.
probes.hazard: A deliberate zero or a deliberate false is dropped. Both invert the caller's intent rather than degrading gracefully: temperature 0 becomes the model's default sampling, and store false becomes store true.

probes.summary: Emit the tools key even when the tool list is empty.
probes.hazard: An empty array is falsy in PHP and truthy in JavaScript and Python, so this is what a direct transliteration produces. The wrong payload is still valid JSON and still gets a response, which is why nothing catches it without a fixture.
probes.note: This set was corrected after measurement. It originally declared only trq-0008, on the mistaken reading that trq-0008 is 'the row with an empty tool list'. It is not — it is the row that DECLARES one explicitly. A request that never calls withTools has an empty tool list too, so every row that does not declare tools carries the hazard: 20 rows, whose complement is exactly the 8 that declare tools, and 20 + 8 = 28 confirms the set is complete. The mutant was deliberately NOT narrowed to match the old declaration; adding a 'withTools was called' flag that exists only to make a probe narrow is precisely the tautology the exact-set design prevents.

probes.summary: Serialize the Any tool-choice member as the string 'any' rather than mapping it to 'required'.
probes.hazard: A port that derives wire strings from enum member names gets every other member right and this one wrong.

probes.summary: Send a tool call's arguments as a JSON object instead of a JSON-encoded string.
probes.hazard: The double encoding is unusual enough that a port is likely to 'fix' it. OpenAI accepts the object and misreads the call.

probes.summary: Append provider-native tools after the caller's tools instead of in front of them.
probes.hazard: Ordering reaches the model and influences selection. Nothing errors; the model just chooses differently, which is the hardest class of divergence to notice in production.

probes.summary: Append system prompts after the conversation instead of prepending them.
probes.hazard: Same shape as provider-tools-last: a valid request that means something different.

probes.summary: Report input_tokens as the prompt count without subtracting the cached tokens.
probes.hazard: Invisible until a request actually hits the prompt cache, at which point the caller's cost reporting silently inflates. Only one row in the corpus has a non-zero cached count, which is exactly why that row exists.
probes.note: atr-0004 is the Anthropic counterpart and the only Anthropic row with a non-zero cached count. It discriminates for the OPPOSITE reason to the OpenAI rows: Anthropic reports cache tokens BESIDE input_tokens rather than inside them, so the correct behaviour there is to subtract NOTHING. A mutant that subtracts breaks it, and a mutant that fails to subtract breaks the OpenAI row -- the two providers pin the two directions of the same mistake.

probes.summary: Drop null-valued fields when serializing a value object for storage.
probes.hazard: The storage-side twin of omit-null-keys. A stored row that omits its unset counters rebuilds into a value object that is not the one that was saved, and the divergence only surfaces on the NEXT provider call.

probes.summary: Drop null-valued fields when serializing a PARSED result, rather than when serializing a value object for storage.
probes.hazard: The same absent-versus-null axis as omit-null-on-serialize, on the other side of the boundary. Kept as a separate probe rather than by widening that one: a probe's declared scope is part of its contract, and broadening the behaviour to match a wider intuition would make the declaration wrong rather than the probe better. Every response row carries a null cache-write counter and a null cost, so every one of them catches it.
probes.note: Declares all seven response rows. trs-0006 is skipped in both ports for an unrelated reason (the empty-map artefact), so the effective expectation is six in each — the loader subtracts skips, because a skipped row cannot fail. The Anthropic rows are declared too: every one of them carries a null somewhere in usage, and atr-0001 exists precisely to assert that a null thought_tokens survives as null. atr-0005 is skipped in both ports for an unrelated reason (G-50, a Length finish raises there and returns in the reference), and the loader subtracts skips because a skipped row cannot fail.

probes.summary: When rebuilding a user message, pass the stored content parts straight back into the constructor.
probes.hazard: The reference's user-message constructor appends a text part built from its own content argument, so doing this appends a second copy and the message text doubles on every save-and-load cycle. A real consumer shipped this. Nothing errors — the conversation just grows.
